items.title: Tyler: England have golden opportunity to win Euro 2028
items.excerpt: Martin Tyler is more convinced than ever he will finally get the chance to commentate on England winning a major international trophy after watching Thomas Tuchel's side's 3-2 Uefa Nations League victory in Spain
body: Martin Tyler is more convinced than ever he will finally get the chance to commentate on England winning a major international trophy after watching Thomas Tuchel's side's 3-2 Uefa Nations League victory in Spain

The legendary football commentator, whose new book 'Tales from the Gantry: Letters from a Lifetime in Football' was published on Monday, knows a thing or two about England teams, good and bad, having called over 350 Three Lions internationals while attending an astonishing 13 World Cup finals during a decorated 53-year career that is still going today.
The book is "historical", says Tyler. "It is what I was thinking about in football that week. There's 110 different essays, half a dozen of them were letters from America.

"I wrote 500 words a week for two and a half years. It starts early in 2004 and finishes in July 2026." items.title: Is Trafford England's new No 1 after Spain heroics?
items.excerpt: Do England have a new No 1? Thomas Tuchel insists not. "There's no No 1," he said. But Jordan Pickford might have his work cut out to wrestle the shirt back from James Trafford on the evidence of his performance in England's 3-2 win over Sp…
body: Do England have a new No 1? Thomas Tuchel insists not. "There's no No 1," he said. But Jordan Pickford might have his work cut out to wrestle the shirt back from James Trafford on the evidence of his performance in England's 3-2 win over Spain.

It felt significant that he started in the first place. Pickford has been England's undisputed first choice for a decade; an outstanding servant to the national team whose total of 94 caps puts him behind only Peter Shilton among the most-capped goalkeepers.

But this was undoubtedly England's biggest test of their Nations League campaign and Tuchel opted for Trafford, encouraged by his displays at home to Spain and away to Czech Republic in September. "He had a brilliant match," he added afterwards.

If it is a changing of the guard, then it is being handled carefully. "I think it's smart management," said Sky Sports' Roy Keane before kick-off in Madrid. "This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing." items.title: England talking points: Tuchel learns Argentina lesson as full-backs shine
items.excerpt: After England beat Spain in their own back yard in a statement result, we look at the main talking points from a memorable moment in Madrid... Bold England show their strengths with front-foot approach
body: After England beat Spain in their own back yard in a statement result, we look at the main talking points from a memorable moment in Madrid... Bold England show their strengths with front-foot approach

England's football DNA has been in focus this autumn. In Madrid, we saw the English style at its best. From the first whistle, England were boldly on the front foot, overwhelming Spain with pace, power and directness.

They snapped into tackles and gave short shrift to their opponents when they called for fouls. It was physical, it was aggressive. It was certainly not England trying to replicate the Spanish style. items.title: Ten-man England hold on to claim famous win over Spain
items.excerpt: England withstood a Spain fightback after Elliot Anderson's red card to secure a famous 3-2 victory and finish above the world champions at the top of their Nations League group.
body: England withstood a Spain fightback after Elliot Anderson's red card to secure a famous 3-2 victory and finish above the world champions at the top of their Nations League group.

Thomas Tuchel's side were sensational for an hour in Madrid, taking the lead when Harry Kane scored a penalty at the end of the first half and then adding quickfire goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.
But a one-sided game was turned on its head when Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal following Jarell Quansah's error, allowing Mikel Oyarzabal to score from the spot.

Spain reduced the deficit to one goal when substitute Nico Williams converted Lamine Yamal's cross after Anthony Gordon had been dispossessed, but England clung on thanks to James Trafford. items.title: Arsenal's wait for home WSL win goes on after Earps masterclass
items.excerpt: Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win continues as they drew 1-1 against London City Lionesses on Sunday - their fifth draw in a row at the Emirates this season - with an inspired Mary Earps denying the Gunners victory.
body: Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win continues as they drew 1-1 against London City Lionesses on Sunday - their fifth draw in a row at the Emirates this season - with an inspired Mary Earps denying the Gunners victory.

While the result extends Arsenal's unbeaten home run to 24 league matches, it is becoming an increasing concern and a spectre on the shoulder that the Gunners have been unable to secure three points at the Emirates this year.

Giving her view to Sky Sports after the game, Renee Slegers - managing her 50th Arsenal game - said: "We spent more time than we normally do without the ball; partly the game plan and partly them asking questions of us on the pitch.
"We create big chances, could have done more with those. That's the frustrating part. This is the fifth [home game] and we couldn't give the fans the win. Unfortunately we couldn't do it for them."
